Documented parent-to-child channels: (a) the spawn prompt Codex writes ('A good subagent prompt should explain how to divide the work, whether Codex should wait for all agents before continuing, and what summary or output to return'); (b) configuration inheritance: 'If you don't configure a subagent model or model_reasoning_effort, the subagent inherits the parent agent's model and reasoning effort'; 'Other session settings, such as sandbox_mode, mcp_servers, and skills.config, inherit from the parent when the custom agent file omits them'; 'Subagents inherit your current sandbox policy'; 'Codex also reapplies the parent turn's live runtime overrides when it spawns a child'; (c) AGENTS.md and skills: 'Codex loads these files as configuration layers for spawned sessions' (custom agent files) and delegation can be triggered 'when applicable AGENTS.md or skill instructions request it'. Built-in agents: default, worker, explorer. Design guidance: 'Keep the main agent focused on requirements, decisions, and final outputs'; 'Return summaries from subagents instead of raw intermediate output.' ChatGPT Work: 'Subagents use the tools available to the parent chat'; Ultra intelligence level 'lets ChatGPT proactively delegate suitable work to subagents'. Auto-review reviewer (separate mechanism, auto-review page): 'The reviewer is itself a Codex agent with a narrower job than the main agent: decide whether a specific boundary-crossing action should run. The reviewer sees a compact transcript plus the exact approval request. That typically includes user messages, surfaced assistant updates, relevant tool calls and tool outputs, and the action now being proposed for approval. It can also perform read-only checks to gather missing context, but it does so rarely. Hidden assistant reasoning is not included. Auto-review sees retained chat items and tool evidence, not private chain-of-thought.' So the reviewer is the one Codex child with a documented (compact, V4-like) transcript view; work subagents remain undocumented. Returned to parent: Consolidated result, not transcript: 'When many agents are running, Codex waits until all requested results are available, then returns a consolidated response'; 'The main thread collects the subagent results into its final response'; the app 'surfaces each subagent thread so you can inspect its work and the summary returned to the main chat'. Approval requests from inactive threads surface to the user (CLI overlay shows the source thread; non-interactive runs fail the action 'and Codex surfaces the error back to the parent workflow'). Auto-review: 'Codex returns the review rationale to the main agent' on denial; reviewer transcripts retained under ~/.codex/sessions. Siblings or ledger: Not documented. No statement that agent threads see, message, or share state with each other; orchestration ('spawning new subagents, routing follow-up instructions, waiting for results, and closing agent threads') is done by the main thread. The user can steer, stop, or close a running subagent by asking Codex; /agent switches threads in the CLI; the web sidebar 'doesn't provide controls to stop or steer an individual subagent'. No shared ledger or peer-status primitive.

harnesses.default_visibility: DEVIN CLI SUBAGENTS (verified): parent conversation: NONE. 'A subagent shares tools and codebase context with the parent, but operates in its own conversation chain -- it does not inherit the parent's conversation history.' 'Subagents run as their own agent sessions, each with its own context window and inference calls.' Parent task: the spawn prompt only ('the run_subagent tool takes a profile, not a model'). Profile descriptions are shown to the parent: 'The agent sees a description of each available profile and chooses the most appropriate one'. Nesting: 'By default, subagents cannot spawn their own subagents — only the root agent can. Subagent tools (run_subagent and read_subagent) are disabled inside a subagent to prevent unbounded nesting'; custom profiles opt in with max-nesting (integer, default none). Background subagents 'inherit any tool permissions you have already granted during the current session'; ask_user_question 'is always withheld from subagents'. MANAGED DEVINS (cloud; advanced-capabilities page): 'delegate them to a team of managed Devins working in parallel, each running in its own isolated VM. The coordinator session scopes the work, monitors progress, resolves conflicts, and compiles results'; the coordinator can 'launch child sessions with specific prompts, playbooks, tags, and ACU limits' and 'send follow-up instructions or clarifications to running sessions'; 'Devin analyzes your request and proposes the sessions for your approval before launching them.' The page never states whether a child sees the coordinator's conversation; documented channels are launch prompt, playbook, tags and follow-up messages (V0/V1-by-prose). DYNAMIC WORKFLOWS page (new): each agent() call 'spawns an agent and waits for its structured output. By default that agent is an independent Devin session on its own VM'; separate-VM child 'cannot see the orchestrating session's files, so code handoffs go through git branches'; shared-VM option 'shares its working tree, including uncommitted changes'. Background: 'The parent is automatically notified when the subagent completes'; if a foreground subagent is backgrounded 'the parent agent's tool call has already returned ... The subagent's result won't feed back into the parent's current pipeline, but you'll be notified when it completes.' Cancelled, failed or completed subagents can be resumed with a new prompt (always foreground). Managed Devins: coordinator 'compiles results'; release note 'Structured Output for Child Sessions' (April 3, 2026): 'Child sessions can return structured JSON via schema for automated workflows'; MCP: 'wait for all of them to finish in a single call instead of polling individually' and 'Inspect any session's full event timeline'. Dynamic workflows: agent(prompt, phase=..., schema=...) 'Runs one agent and returns its structured output as a dict'; failed or invalid output is handled by the script (skip, default, retry, fail). harnesses.name: Goose (goose-docs.ai; block.github.io/goose now redirects there): subagents through the summon platform extension (delegate and load tools; recipes, sub_recipes and custom agents as delegation sources)
harnesses.default_visibility: NONE by documented mechanism: the child runs in its own session with only the delegate call's instructions or source (recipe, subrecipe or custom agent) plus parameters; extensions are inherited. Custom Agents page: 'Delegated subagents run in isolated sessions and do not automatically inherit the full parent conversation.' Subrecipes page: 'Sub-recipe sessions run in isolation - they don't share conversation history, memory, or state with the main recipe or other subrecipes.' The Subagents page is looser ('Internal subagents spawn goose instances to handle tasks using your current session's context and extensions.') but its Default Settings table lists only Extensions as 'Inherited from parent'. Returns: Return Mode defaults to 'Full Details (Default): See all tool executions and reasoning steps' versus 'Summary Only: Get just the final result to keep your conversation clean'; 'If a subagent fails or times out (5-minute default), you will receive no output from that subagent.'; async delegation 'returns a task id' and load(source: task id) 'waits for the result'.
harnesses.quote: s instructions or source (recipe, subrecipe or custom agent) plus parameters; extensions are inherited. Custom Agents page:
harnesses.knob: none documented for passing the parent conversation to the child. What exists: delegate(instructions: ...) or delegate(source: ...) carries the assignment; sub_recipes values pre-set parameters ('Pre-set values take precedence over context-based parameters') while the parent model fills the rest from its own context; load(source: ...) goes the other way (pulls an agent's or recipe's instructions into the current conversation instead of delegating); Return Mode (natural language) and delegate(..., async: true) change what and when the parent gets back; the subagent_system.md prompt template customizes the child's system prompt; GOOSE_SUBAGENT_MAX_TURNS and settings.max_turns cap turns
harnesses.notes: partially_verified. Q4 only half answered: the prompt-templates page lists subagent_system.md as 'System prompt for subagents spawned to handle specific tasks' (so the child runs under a subagent-specific system prompt) but its content is only linked to the GitHub source, not reproduced in the docs. Q1 to Q3 answered. Subagents cannot nest ('Subagent spawning: Cannot create additional subagents to prevent infinite recursion') and are disabled outside autonomous permission mode. New row.

harnesses.name: Windsurf, now Devin Desktop (docs.windsurf.com 307-redirects to docs.devin.ai): Cascade (Fast Context retrieval subagent, workflows, one-click delegation to cloud Devin) and the Devin Local agent's subagents (run_subagent and read_subagent tools, profiles subagent_explore and subagent_general, custom agents/<name>.md profiles)
harnesses.default_visibility: Two agents. Cascade (legacy): no general delegation, 'plugins and subagents have no Cascade equivalent at all'; its only subagent is Fast Context, auto-triggered for retrieval: 'When Cascade receives a query that requires code search, Fast Context will trigger automatically.' What Fast Context receives beyond the query is not stated. Workflows are not delegation: 'Upon invocation, Cascade sequentially processes each step defined in the Workflow'. Cloud Devin gets the plan: 'work on a plan with a local agent and, with a single click, send it to Devin for implementation'. Devin Local (default local agent, same harness as Devin CLI): NONE by documented mechanism. The child gets the parent's prompt, tools and repo, not the transcript: 'A subagent shares tools and codebase context with the parent', it 'operates in its own conversation chain', 'it does not inherit the parent's conversation history'. Background subagents also inherit session tool grants: 'Background subagents inherit any tool permissions you have already granted during the current session.' ask_user_question 'is always withheld from subagents'; run_subagent and read_subagent are disabled inside a subagent unless max-nesting is set.
harnesses.quote: plugins and subagents have no Cascade equivalent at all
harnesses.knob: No knob changes what the child sees of the parent conversation; the parent's prompt is the only channel (a finished subagent 'can be resumed with a new prompt'). Documented switches: subagents_enabled (user config.json; false removes the run_subagent and read_subagent tools), the Subagents (Preview) toggle in Devin Settings, the org Default subagent model setting (Subagent router, a specific model, or None which disables subagents), profile choice by the parent (subagent_explore: read-only plus web search on the default subagent model; subagent_general: full tools in the foreground, pre-approved tools only in the background, parent's model), foreground vs background, and custom profile frontmatter name, description, model, allowed-tools, max-nesting. Cascade side: none documented (Fast Context has no setting on its page; workflows are markdown step lists).
harnesses.notes: partially_verified. New row. Not answered by the pages: whether a Devin Local subagent is told it is a subagent (built-in profile prompts are not published; the custom-profile example is user-authored text such as 'report findings back to the parent agent'), and what Fast Context receives from Cascade. Returns: 'When a subagent finishes, the parent agent reads the result and summarizes the key findings and actions for you.' 'You do not see the subagent's raw output directly.' Background: 'The parent is automatically notified when the subagent completes.' A subagent moved to the background mid-run: 'The subagent's result won't feed back into the parent's current pipeline'. Fast Context returns 'targeted results'. Cloud Devin returns PRs reviewed in the editor. Quick Review is a separate review subagent that 'analyzes the diff' (Devin Local only). Devin Local is the default for new tabs; Cascade is still selectable.

harnesses.name: JetBrains Junie: Junie CLI custom subagents (.junie/agents/*.md or .agents/*.md with YAML frontmatter, auto-delegated by name and description; no subagent feature is documented for the Junie IDE plugin)
harnesses.default_visibility: NONE by documented mechanism. The child runs on its own system prompt (the file's prompt body) plus the task the main agent delegates: 'This prompt will be added to the instructions delegated from the main agent.' It does not get the main conversation: 'The subagent then works independently in its own context and returns the result to the main agent.' and subagents keep 'the subagent's context out of the main conversation'. With allowPromptArgument true, 'the delegated user request is appended automatically as User Input' when $prompt is not referenced in the body. The pages never enumerate what 'instructions delegated' contain (task text only, or excerpts of history).
harnesses.quote: s prompt body) plus the task the main agent delegates:
harnesses.knob: allowPromptArgument (exposes $prompt, the delegated user request, to the subagent prompt) and prompt-body variables such as $path and $focus are the only documented context levers; nothing passes the parent transcript. Other frontmatter: tools (allowlist of tool groups Read, Bash, Glob, Grep, Write, Edit, WebSearch, AskUserQuestion), disallowedTools, mcpServers, model, reasoningLevel (alias effort), maxTurns, skills, permissionMode (default, acceptEdits, dontAsk, bypassPermissions, plan). Session policy: /settings then Subagents, SameModelOnly or Auto (default), saved in ~/.junie/settings.json (Early Access).
harnesses.notes: partially_verified. New row. Not answered by the pages: whether the subagent is told it is a subagent (the user is: 'Junie CLI invokes subagents automatically, informing the user which subagent has started working on the task.'). Returns: the main agent 'runs it as a subtask, and brings the result back into the main session'; subagent transcripts are written to the session's subagents folder (Ctrl+O opens them). Subagents 'cannot be invoked manually via slash commands'. Junie also imports .claude/agents, .cursor/agents and .codex/agents files.

harnesses.name: Replit Agent (Agent 4, current): task system background tasks (each task gets its own Agent and thread in an isolated project copy); no user-facing sub-agent, 'extended thinking' or parallel-agent API is documented on docs.replit.com
harnesses.default_visibility: A selection of state, not the parent conversation by any documented statement: the task worker receives the approved task brief and the project. 'Background tasks are separate threads where Agent works independently in isolated copies of your project.' 'Each task also gets its own Agent and inherits your full project context, so you don't repeat yourself.' Before it starts a task holds 'the task title, description, and plan' (the plan lists scope, implementation steps, definition of done, relevant files, agent mode). Threads: 'each background task gets its own thread' 'so Agent can keep task work isolated without mixing up the conversations.' Whether 'full project context' includes the main-thread transcript is not stated.
harnesses.quote: Background tasks are separate threads where Agent works independently in isolated copies of your project.
harnesses.knob: none documented that changes what the task's Agent sees. Levers that shape the brief: View plan, Revise plan, Accept tasks or Start building, Plan mode task lists; concurrency by plan (Starter none, Core 1, Pro 10, Enterprise 64); dependencies detected by Agent. Effort (Low to Max, per model) and Agent modes (Free, Power, Max) set reasoning and cost, not context. The Agent 3 'Extended Thinking' and 'High Power' toggles no longer appear anywhere on docs.replit.com (site-wide llms-full.txt has no 'extended thinking', 'high power' or 'subagent'); only App Testing's 'Extended Autonomy' and an internal 'parallel multi-agent search' for warehouse queries remain.
harnesses.notes: partially_verified. New row. Not answered by the pages: whether the task's Agent is told it is a delegated task, and whether the main thread's conversation is part of 'full project context'. Returns go to the user, not to a parent agent: 'When a task finishes, Agent shows you what it did: the work log, test results, and a live preview of the changes.' You Apply or Dismiss; 'Agent handles conflict resolution automatically when applying changes from multiple tasks.' After apply the main chat carries 'the implementation summary, checks, warnings'. Agent 4 changelog: 'Run tasks in parallel: Agent handles multiple tasks at once so you can move faster'.

harnesses.name: Manus: Wide Research (the main agent decomposes a task into sub-tasks and deploys parallel sub-agents; automatically triggered)
harnesses.default_visibility: NONE by documented mechanism: each sub-agent starts in a fresh context that holds only its decomposed sub-task (one item), not the parent's conversation: 'Each agent receives its own dedicated context and processes one item independently.' and 'Each sub-task is assigned to a dedicated agent with its own fresh context window'. The parent does the decomposition: 'The main agent analyzes your request and breaks it into independent sub-tasks (e.g., "research company #1", "research company #2", etc.)'. Returns: 'The main agent collects all completed sub-tasks and assembles them into your requested format (table, report, dataset, etc.)'. Scale (help center): 'Wide Research can run 20 subtasks simultaneously, equivalent to having 20 Agents helping with one task.'
harnesses.quote: s conversation:
harnesses.knob: none documented: no setting changes what a sub-agent sees, and the feature cannot even be invoked by hand: 'This feature only supports automatic triggering.' (help center). The only documented sub-agent control is the model tier: in Manus 1.6 MAX 'all sub-Agents performing "Wide Research" use a more advanced model architecture' (changes the model, not visibility). Each sub-task's credit use is capped at 50 credits.
harnesses.doc_url: https://manus.im/docs/features/wide-research ; https://help.manus.im/en/articles/11960169-what-is-wide-research ; https://manus.im/docs/llms.txt (docs index: no other sub-agent or delegation page)
harnesses.notes: partially_verified. Q1 (fresh per-item context), Q2 (no knob, automatic trigger only) and Q3 (main agent collects and assembles results) answered; Q4 (whether the sub-agent is told it is orchestrated) is not addressed on either page. The docs index lists no other delegation page (the Manus API page only points to open.manus.im). New row.

harnesses.name: Dify: Agent node in Workflow/Chatflow (classic Agent node: LLM plus Dify tools, including a Workflow published as a tool; new Agent node (beta): invite a published Agent and give it an 'Agent task') and Workflow as Tool
harnesses.default_visibility: NONE by documented mechanism. New Agent node: the invited agent receives only the task text written in 'Agent task' (plus upstream variables pulled in with '/', as text, and files): 'There you set only the task you want done.' and 'This is separate from the agent's own prompt and capabilities.'; 'Variables you pull in reach the agent as text and are truncated at 2,000 characters.'; runs are isolated: 'nothing from one node's run (files it wrote, tools it installed) carries into another'. Returns: 'By default, an Agent node returns a single output, text: the agent's reply to its task, as one block of text.' plus declared outputs (files capped at 50 MB). Workflow as Tool (callable from the classic Agent node, Agent apps or another workflow): the child workflow receives only the tool parameters, that is its User Input fields: 'Turn any Workflow that starts with a User Input node into a tool, so you can reuse multi-step logic across apps.'; it returns its Output node variables: 'Each output variable name becomes a key in the tool's result, accessible to the parent workflow that invokes the tool.' The classic Agent node itself sees only its Instruction, its Query ('Query specifies the user input or task the Agent should work on.') and a bounded history window ('Memory controls how many previous messages the Agent remembers using TokenBufferMemory.').
harnesses.quote: (plus upstream variables pulled in with
harnesses.knob: New Agent node: the 'Agent task' field (type '/' to pull in outputs from earlier nodes, truncated at 2,000 characters as text; 'To hand over longer content in full, pass it as a file: the agent receives the whole file and reads it in its sandbox.') and 'New output' declarations for what comes back. Classic Agent node: the 'Memory' window (how much prior conversation the agent node sees) and the per-tool parameter mode ('auto-generated' parameters are populated by the Agent, 'manual input' parameters are fixed in the tool configuration), which decides what a called workflow-tool receives. No agent-to-agent handoff or agent-as-tool parameter is documented.
harnesses.notes: partially_verified. Q1, Q2 and Q3 answered for both paths (Agent node and Workflow as Tool); Q4 (whether the invited agent or called workflow is told it is orchestrated) is not addressed. The new Agent node 'is in beta and available in Workflow apps only', so there is no chat history to pass; the classic Agent node page documents tools but no sub-agent feature, and the new Agent's tool types ('plugins, custom APIs, workflows, and MCP servers') include no agent type. New row.

harnesses.name: n8n: AI Agent Tool sub-node (agent as tool, nestable), Call n8n Workflow Tool sub-node (sub-workflow as tool, paired with the Execute Sub-workflow Trigger's Input data mode) and Agents (Preview) Sub-agents
harnesses.default_visibility: NONE by documented mechanism: the child receives only the tool-call input. AI Agent Tool: its own 'Prompt (User Message)' (static text, an expression, or a value the parent model fills through $fromAI()) plus its own 'System Message'; no page passes the parent's conversation or memory sub-node: 'Prompt (User Message): The prompt to the LLM explaining what actions to perform and what information to return.'; 'System Message: A message to send to the agent before the conversation starts.'; 'This allows you to use multiple agents in a single workflow without the complexity of managing context and variables that sub-workflows require.' Call n8n Workflow Tool: the sub-workflow receives only the 'Workflow Inputs' defined by its trigger's schema: 'The Call n8n Workflow Tool node is a tool that allows an agent to run another n8n workflow and fetch its output data.'; model-filled values are drawn from the parent's context: 'The AI model will use the context from the task and information from other connected tools to fill in the appropriate details.' Returns: the sub-agent's final output (intermediate steps only when 'Return Intermediate Steps' is on); for sub-workflows 'The last node of Workflow B sends the data back to the Execute Sub-workflow node in Workflow A.' and 'The error text is returned to the agent as the tool result.' Agents (Preview): 'Sub-agents let this agent hand off work to other published agents.' with no statement of what is handed over.
harnesses.quote: Prompt (User Message)
harnesses.knob: $fromAI(key, description, type, defaultValue) in 'Prompt (User Message)' or in 'Workflow Inputs' (or the 'Let the model define this parameter' button) lets the parent model decide what the child receives; the sub-workflow trigger's 'Input data mode' ('Define using fields below', 'Define using JSON example', 'Accept all data') fixes the input schema; 'Automatically Passthrough Binary Images' forwards binary images to the sub-agent as image messages; 'Return Intermediate Steps' and 'Require Specific Output Format' shape what returns. Agents (Preview): only 'When should this agent be used?' (a delegation description) and a maximum number of sub-agents running in parallel; no context setting.
harnesses.notes: partially_verified. Q2 and Q3 answered; Q1 is answered only by the parameter inventory (the pages list Prompt (User Message) and System Message as the sub-agent's inputs and never state in words that the parent's history or memory is withheld); Q4 (whether the child is told it is orchestrated) is not addressed; for Agents (Preview) Sub-agents the page documents the hand-off but not what is passed. New row.

venues.recommendation: Post to arXiv (cs.AI, cross-list cs.MA and cs.CL) by 2026-10-31, then make one submission to TMLR in the first week of November 2026: it is rolling, free, Scopus- and DBLP-indexed, judges on technical correctness rather than perceived significance, lets you run the full six-level design, both models, and the deployable policy table at whatever length they need, and permits the preprint. The only conference that beats it on topical fit is AAMAS 2027's GAAI track (paper due 2026-10-08, Hanoi, ACM DL/Scopus-indexed, arXiv allowed, Findings fallback), but that lands before your preprint date and is achievable only if the manuscript is essentially finished today; ARR's October cycle (2026-10-12, NAACL 2027 decision 2027-02-10) has the same timing problem plus a 9-month TACL embargo if it fails. If you want a conference rather than a journal after the preprint, the honest choice is ARR January 2027 to ACL 2027 Kyoto, with the caveat that only the month is published. Non-archival companions that do not consume the paper: the AAAI-27 workshop round (2026-11-20, list not yet public), ICLR 2027 workshops (projected late January 2027, not yet announced), and the 2027 successor of NeurIPS's Meta Agents workshop, which is the closest match to your question. Dates I could not confirm: the exact ARR January 2027 deadline, any ICLR 2027 workshop date, everything about COLM 2027 and AIES 2027, AAMAS 2027 workshop deadlines, TMLR and TACL turnaround times, and PeerJ's indexing and JAIR's Scopus listing (both official pages returned 403 today). ICLR 2027's 2026-09-25 deadline is confirmed but is not a realistic solo target from a standing start.

critic.summary: Judged from the listing alone (nothing fetched). Cluster counts are healthy (C1 16, C2 21, C3 14, C4 12+2, C5 14, C6 16, C7 10+2, C8 10, C9 24, C10 14, C11 44) and all twelve required labs have at least one primary source, but Google DeepMind is anchored only by an optional social-simulation library (Concordia) plus untagged entries, and Thinking Machines is covered by an inference-determinism note that says nothing about agents. The largest structural problem is merge orphans: at least six papers were explicitly deferred by one cluster owner to another cluster and never adopted there (When Context Hurts 2605.04361 flagged 'probably a must' for C2; Do More Agents Help 2606.05670 for C10; constraint drift 2605.10481, AgentMisalignment 2506.04018 and Reward Hacking Benchmark 2605.02964 for C5; LLMs Get Lost in Multi-Turn 2505.06120 for C6). Substantive absences: the practitioner counter-position to Anthropic's post (Cognition, Don't Build Multi-Agents), Google's AI co-scientist and Chain of Agents as DeepMind/Google orchestrator-worker primaries, Hammond et al. Multi-Agent Risks, the multi-agent-debate origin papers, any prompt-injection or instruction-vs-data anchor (V3 to V5 inject text authored by other agents), the OpenAI Model Spec and Anthropic constitution as primary hierarchy definitions, C9 classics that map directly onto V0/V1/V3/V5 (Parnas 1972, March and Simon 1958 uncertainty absorption, Holmstrom and Milgrom 1991 multitask, Thompson 1967, Brooks 1975), and every statistics reference a six-level dose-response with binary verdicts needs (trend test, multiplicity correction, eval error bars, mixed models). Suspicious metadata: geng2026illusion (arXiv Feb 2025), perrow2000normal (1984/1999, never 2000), hackman2004leading (a 4-page journal note masquerading as the 2002 book), an arXiv-year versus venue-year convention split across keys, and a cluster of web entries carrying scraped browser titles, breadcrumbs, or repo taglines. Only one true duplicate pair: the two Meta Muse Spark 1.3 entries, both marked must.

gaps.what_is_missing: When Context Hurts: The Crossover Effect of Knowledge Transfer on Multi-Agent Design Exploration (Vigraham, 2026, arXiv 2605.04361). The C1 rejection note says it 'belongs in the context-visibility cluster, where it is probably a must', yet C2 never adopted it. It is a 2,700-run empirical result that artifact handoff between agents degrades exploration on some tasks, the closest empirical neighbour to a worker-side context dose.
gaps.suggested_action: Add to C2 as must. Resolve via https://export.arxiv.org/api/query?id_list=2605.04361 and cite it in the gap statement alongside patel2026dynamic; it manipulates what a downstream agent receives, so state explicitly why it is not a dose-response on hierarchical visibility.

gaps.what_is_missing: Three papers deferred to this cluster by other owners and never adopted: Safe Multi-Agent Behavior Must Be Maintained, Not Merely Asserted: Constraint Drift in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems (arXiv 2605.10481, deferred from C8); AgentMisalignment: Measuring the Propensity for Misaligned Behaviour in LLM-Based Agents (arXiv 2506.04018, deferred from C8); Reward Hacking Benchmark: Measuring Exploits in LLM Agents with Tool Use (Thaman, ICML 2026, arXiv 2605.02964, held back 'if a specification-gaming-in-agents slot opens'). The last one measures literal objective versus intent, which is the paper's primary outcome in a different costume.
gaps.suggested_action: Query https://export.arxiv.org/api/query?id_list=2605.10481,2506.04018,2605.02964. Take 2605.02964 as should (it is the agentic successor to krakovna2020specification) and 2605.10481 as should (constraint drift in MAS is the negative-space version of DEVIATED); 2506.04018 optional.

gaps.what_is_missing: Do More Agents Help? Controlled and Protocol-Aligned Evaluation of LLM Agent Workflows (Fu et al., 2026, arXiv 2606.05670), deferred from C1 to 'the evaluation cluster' and absent from C10. Also TRAIL (arXiv 2505.08638), deferred from C3 to evaluation, absent.
gaps.suggested_action: Query https://export.arxiv.org/api/query?id_list=2606.05670,2505.08638. Add 2606.05670 as should: a controlled MAS-versus-single-agent evaluation protocol is the methodological sibling of the paper's fixed-harness design. TRAIL optional.

gaps.what_is_missing: LLMs Get Lost In Multi-Turn Conversation (Laban et al., 2025, arXiv 2505.06120), deferred from C2 to 'an instruction-following cluster' and absent from C6.
gaps.suggested_action: Query https://export.arxiv.org/api/query?id_list=2505.06120; add as optional in C6 if the paper discusses underspecified worker instructions or the FLAGGED verdict.

gaps.area: C6-hierarchy: primary definitions of the hierarchy
gaps.what_is_missing: No first-party document that defines the instruction hierarchy the paper's workers are trained under. OpenAI Model Spec (chain of command: platform > developer > user > guideline; model-spec.openai.com, first published May 2024, revised through 2025) and Anthropic's constitution (anthropic.com/constitution, January 2026; explicit principal hierarchy Anthropic > operators > users) are both absent. wallace2024hierarchy is the training paper, not the policy document.
gaps.suggested_action: Fetch https://model-spec.openai.com/ (cite the dated revision) and https://www.anthropic.com/constitution; add both to C6 and tag C11-labs-us. Optional companion: OpenAI, Practices for Governing Agentic AI Systems (Shavit et al., Dec 2023, openai.com/research/practices-for-governing-agentic-ai-systems) for C8.

gaps.what_is_missing: V3, V4 and V5 place text authored by other agents (sibling mandates, orchestrator ledger, peer progress) inside the worker's context. Whether a model treats such text as data or as instructions is the prompt-injection and instruction/data-separation literature, and it is entirely absent: no Greshake et al. 2023 (indirect prompt injection, arXiv 2302.12173), no SEP benchmark (Zverev et al., Can LLMs Separate Instructions From Data?, ICLR 2025, arXiv 2403.06833), no AgentDojo (Debenedetti et al., NeurIPS 2024, arXiv 2406.13352), no LLM-to-LLM injection in MAS (Prompt Infection, Lee and Tiwari, 2024, arXiv 2410.07283). Reviewers will ask why deviation under V4 is not simply injection.
gaps.suggested_action: Query https://export.arxiv.org/api/query?id_list=2302.12173,2403.06833,2406.13352,2410.07283. Take Zverev (should) and one of Greshake or AgentDojo (should); Prompt Infection optional as the MAS-specific case.

gaps.what_is_missing: The only C11-tagged DeepMind item is vezhnevets2023concordia (optional), which the C10 rejection note itself calls a social-simulation library, not a task system. Google's actual orchestrator-worker primaries are absent: Towards an AI co-scientist (Gottweis et al., Feb 2025, arXiv 2502.18864; supervisor agent dispatching generation, reflection, ranking, evolution, proximity and meta-review workers, with a documented task queue that determines what each worker sees), Chain of Agents (Zhang et al., NeurIPS 2024, arXiv 2406.02818; sequential workers each shown only their chunk plus a communication unit), AlphaEvolve (Novikov et al., June 2025, arXiv 2506.13131). Also, DeepMind-authored entries already in the base (shah2022goalmisgeneralization, krakovna2020specification, tomasev2026delegation, kim2025scaling) carry no C11 tag, so lab coverage cannot be audited from tags.
gaps.suggested_action: Query https://export.arxiv.org/api/query?id_list=2502.18864,2406.02818,2506.13131. Add the co-scientist as must in C1 and C11; Chain of Agents as should. Add the C11-labs-us tag to the four existing DeepMind entries. Optional: Google Antigravity agent-manager docs (antigravity.google, Nov 2025) as a Google sub-agent primary.

gaps.what_is_missing: Cognition AI, Don't Build Multi-Agents (Walden Yan, June 2025, cognition.ai/blog/dont-build-multi-agents). It is the direct rebuttal to hadfield2025multiagent and states the paper's hypothesis verbatim: sub-agents that do not see the parent's full trace make conflicting implicit decisions, so 'share context, share full agent traces'. A worker-side visibility dose is the experiment that adjudicates this disagreement, and the base cites only one side of it.
gaps.suggested_action: Fetch https://cognition.ai/blog/dont-build-multi-agents; add as must in C2 (tag C1). Optional companions: Manus, Context Engineering for AI Agents: Lessons from Building Manus (Yichao Ji, July 2025, manus.im/blog) and LangChain deepagents subagent docs (context quarantine).

gaps.area: C3-failures: risk report and debate origins
gaps.what_is_missing: Hammond et al., Multi-Agent Risks from Advanced AI (Cooperative AI Foundation technical report, Feb 2025, arXiv 2502.14143) is absent; it is the canonical taxonomy (miscoordination, conflict, collusion, information asymmetries) that MAST-style empirical work is positioned against. The debate-failure line (wynn2025talk, chen2025debate, hao2026flips) cites no debate origin: Du et al., Improving Factuality and Reasoning through Multiagent Debate (ICML 2024, arXiv 2305.14325) and Liang et al., Encouraging Divergent Thinking through Multi-Agent Debate (EMNLP 2024, arXiv 2305.19118).
gaps.suggested_action: Query https://export.arxiv.org/api/query?id_list=2502.14143,2305.14325,2305.19118. Hammond as must in C3 or C8; Du as should; Liang optional. Optional scaling counterpoint to kim2025scaling: More Agents Is All You Need (Li et al., TMLR 2024, arXiv 2402.05120) and If Multi-Agent Debate is the Answer, What is the Question? (arXiv 2502.08788).

gaps.what_is_missing: The base can produce a prediction per level, but the sharpest classics for four of the six levels are absent. V0 (nothing): Parnas 1972, On the Criteria To Be Used in Decomposing Systems into Modules (information hiding; CACM 15(12), DOI 10.1145/361598.361623). V1 (one-sentence objective): March and Simon 1958, Organizations (uncertainty absorption: only inferences travel up and down the hierarchy, not the evidence). V3 (sibling mandates): Holmstrom and Milgrom 1991, Multitask Principal-Agent Analyses (JLEO 7, DOI 10.1093/jleo/7.special_issue.24; visibility of other tasks induces effort substitution). V5 (peer polling): Thompson 1967, Organizations in Action (pooled versus reciprocal interdependence) and Brooks 1975, The Mythical Man-Month (n(n-1)/2 communication cost). Optional V1 frame: mission command and commander's intent (US Army ADP 6-0, 2019; Shattuck 2000, Military Review).
gaps.suggested_action: Crossref: https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1145/361598.361623 and https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1093/jleo/7.special_issue.24. March and Simon, Thompson and Brooks are books not in Crossref; cite by ISBN (March and Simon 2nd ed. Blackwell 1993, ISBN 0631186314; Thompson McGraw-Hill 1967; Brooks Addison-Wesley 1975, anniversary ed. 1995 ISBN 0201835959). Parnas and Holmstrom-Milgrom should be must; the books should.

gaps.what_is_missing: A six-level ordered dose with a binary primary outcome and five secondary outcomes cites no statistical methodology: no trend test for proportions across ordered doses, no multiplicity correction across secondary outcomes, no reference for evaluation uncertainty or clustered errors across probes and seeds, no mixed-model reference. mustahsan2025stochasticity covers ICC only.
gaps.suggested_action: Add Armitage 1955, Tests for Linear Trends in Proportions and Frequencies (Biometrics 11, DOI 10.2307/3001775) and Cochran 1954 (DOI 10.2307/3001616); Benjamini and Hochberg 1995 (DOI 10.1111/j.2517-6161.1995.tb02031.x); Miller 2024, Adding Error Bars to Evals (Anthropic, arXiv 2411.00640; also an Anthropic primary); Bowyer et al. 2025, Position: Don't Use the CLT in LLM Evals With Fewer Than a Few Hundred Datapoints (ICML 2025, arXiv 2503.01747); lme4 (Bates et al. 2015, DOI 10.18637/jss.v067.i01) if mixed logistic models are fitted.

gaps.what_is_missing: Deviation toward an inferred orchestrator objective is plausibly sycophancy toward the principal, and the sycophancy anchor is absent: Sharma et al., Towards Understanding Sycophancy in Language Models (ICLR 2024, arXiv 2310.13548). Alignment Faking (Greenblatt et al., Dec 2024, arXiv 2412.14093) is the strongest evidence that a model that infers its situation from context changes behaviour strategically; absent.
gaps.suggested_action: Query https://export.arxiv.org/api/query?id_list=2310.13548,2412.14093. Sharma should (C7 or C5); alignment faking optional in C5.

gaps.what_is_missing: The rejection note claims no Meta-authored multi-agent preprint exists. Meta FAIR has at least two: ARE: Scaling Up Agent Environments and Evaluations / Gaia2 (Sept 2025, arXiv 2509.17158) and Collaborative Reasoner (April 2025, arXiv 2504.15185). Neither is required for lab coverage (Muse entries suffice) but ARE is a natural C10 citation and corrects a false negative in the record.
gaps.suggested_action: Query https://export.arxiv.org/api/query?id_list=2509.17158,2504.15185; add ARE to C10 as optional and amend the rejection note.

gaps.what_is_missing: Magentic-UI was left unresolved after HTTP 429s on title search; the identifier was never tried.
gaps.suggested_action: Retry with the id, not the title: https://export.arxiv.org/api/query?id_list=2507.22358 (Magentic-UI: Towards Human-in-the-loop Agentic Systems, Mozannar et al., July 2025). Optional in C1.

gaps.what_is_missing: Contract Net and Hearsay-II are present, but the DAI classic on how much of other agents' plans an agent should see (the V4/V5 question) is absent: Durfee and Lesser 1991, Partial Global Planning (IEEE TSMC 21(5), DOI 10.1109/21.120067); Lesser and Corkill 1981, Functionally Accurate, Cooperative Distributed Systems (DOI 10.1109/TSMC.1981.4308581).
gaps.suggested_action: Crossref https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1109/21.120067; add Durfee and Lesser as should, Lesser and Corkill optional.

suspicious_entries.why: Control Illusion: The Failure of Instruction Hierarchies in Large Language Models is arXiv 2502.15851, posted February 2025. Year 2026 is wrong unless a 2026 venue is being cited; if so the venue must appear in the entry.
Normal Accidents was published 1984 (Basic Books) and reissued 1999 (Princeton University Press, with afterword). 2000 matches neither edition.

DOI 10.1108/13527590410545081 is a four-page note in Team Performance Management 10(3/4), not the 2002 book Leading Teams: Setting the Stage for Great Performances (Harvard Business School Press). If the bib renders it as the book, year and publisher are wrong; either way it is a weak substitute for the 1987 'design of work teams' chapter.
ConInstruct is arXiv 2511.14342 (November 2025). 2026 is defensible only as the AAAI 2026 venue year; make sure the entry carries that venue.
Conformity in Large Language Models is arXiv 2410.12428 (October 2024). 2025 is defensible only as the ACL 2025 venue year (moderate confidence on the venue).
Intelligent AI Delegation (Tomasev et al., DeepMind) may have been posted to arXiv in late 2025; low confidence, verify the year and add the C11-labs-us tag either way.
Adaptive Distraction: Probing LLM Contextual Robustness with Automated Tree Search may be a December 2024 arXiv posting; low confidence, check the year.

Year-convention split: this key and zhang2024agentprune use the arXiv year (ICLR 2024 and ICLR 2025 papers respectively) while hong2024metagpt, qian2024chatdev, chen2024agentverse and liu2024lost use the venue year for 2023 arXiv postings. IEEE style will expose the inconsistency; pick one convention and regenerate keys.
Title 'Extending and automating' is a section heading, not a document title; supply the full page title and URL, or fold it into meta2026musecode.

Title 'Muse Spark 1.3 | Meta' is a scraped browser title. Same defect in zai2026glm53 ('GLM-5.3 - Overview - Z.AI DEVELOPER DOCUMENT'), microsoft2026handoff and microsoft2026magentic (breadcrumb titles), xai2026multiagent ('Model Capabilities - Multi Agent'), and the repo taglines used as titles in qwenteam2026qwenagent (contains '>=' and 'etc.'), tencenthunyuan2026hy3 and bytedance2026deerflow. Normalize to document titles before the .bib is rendered.
DeerFlow was first released by ByteDance in May 2025; a 2026 year is right only if the cited version or access date is 2026. State the version.
Repository has existed since 2023; 2026 must be an access year, which should then be applied consistently to every URL-type entry.
